Need the setup/team specifics. Let me check the install/quickstart pages.

It's both. Some setup is done once for the repo and shared through Git, and some has to be done by each person on their own machine.

**Done once, shared with everyone:**
- **Project settings.** `entire enable` creates `.entire/settings.json` and `.entire/.gitignore`. The quickstart says these exist "so collaborators share project settings." Commit them and everyone gets the same config. Personal overrides go in `.entire/settings.local.json`, which stays on your machine.
- **The mirror.** `entire repo mirror add` sets up the regional mirror of the GitHub repo once. The Entire GitHub App also needs access to the repo, and an org admin may have to approve that, but only once.
- **Checkpoint data.** Checkpoints are stored in the repo itself, under `refs/entire/checkpoints/` (or on a shared `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch in older setups). Commits point to them with an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer, so anyone who fetches can see sessions other people captured.

**Each person, on their own machine:**
- **Install the CLI** (e.g. `brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire`).
- **Connect it to their agent.** "Entire installs hooks that capture your agent's work and link it to Git commits." Git hooks live in `.git/hooks`, which Git never shares. So I'd expect each person to run `entire enable` (or the setup command for their agent) in their own clone, even if the settings file is already committed. The docs don't say this outright, so that part is my inference.
- **`entire login`**: each person signs in with their own account.
- **Add the remote**: `entire repo remote add entire` (or `... origin --override`) in each clone, because Git remotes aren't shared either.
- **Linking commits**: when someone commits after an agent session, Entire asks whether to link the commit. Answering "always" saves that choice, but only for that person.

**In short:** one person enables Entire, commits `.entire/`, creates the mirror and gets the GitHub App approved. After that, each teammate installs the CLI, runs `entire login` and `entire enable` in their clone, and adds the `entire` remote. Anyone who skips their part won't have their sessions captured, but they can still see everyone else's checkpoints once they fetch.

Sources: [Quickstart](https://docs.entire.com/quickstart), [FAQ](https://docs.entire.com/faq).

Entire is a Git hosting service built for AI coding agents. It hosts your code like GitHub does, and it also saves the agent sessions that produced each change: the prompt, the transcript, the tool calls and the reasoning.

**Main features:**

- **Session storage (checkpoints).** When an agent's work gets committed, Entire links that commit to the session behind it. Later you can trace any change back to why it was made: what was asked, which files the agent looked at, what commands it ran and what it decided. Secrets are redacted on your machine before anything is stored.
- **Fast Git hosting.** Agents clone, fetch and push much more than people do, especially when several run in parallel. Entire claims pushes are up to 89× faster than GitHub, and it offers hosting regions in the US, EU, Australia and India, which also helps with data-residency rules.
- **GitHub mirroring.** You don't have to leave GitHub. Entire can mirror a GitHub repo, so agents clone and push through Entire while GitHub stays the main copy. Your branch protection and review rules still apply. With "Entire-native branches," you can keep pushing even during a GitHub outage.
- **Agentic search.** One query searches code, commits and past agent sessions, so an agent can find earlier work and the reasoning behind it instead of figuring it out again.
- **Semantic graph (`entire-graph`).** A local, open-source map of the symbols in your codebase and how they relate. Agents can look things up there instead of grepping through files, and Entire claims this cuts token use by up to 71%.
- **Works with many agents.** Supported agents include Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, Gemini/Antigravity, OpenCode and others. The CLI is open source (MIT).

**Useful commands:**
- `entire checkpoint list`: see recent checkpoints.
- `entire why <line>`: shows the commit, prompt and session behind a line of code.
- `entire blame`: like `git blame`, but marks each line's commit as AI, human or mixed. This is per commit, not per line.
- Recap and review commands help check agent-written changes before merging.

In short, Git normally records what changed. Entire also records why, and keeps it searchable for both people and agents.
